_comment: The test piano's instruments and rooms (piano_render). Installed by `python -m piano_render fetch` (piano_render/fetch.py) under root/<subdir>; files are relative to root. label = what the Room page shows: plain and honest about what was sampled. engine: sfizz (SFZ via libsfizz), fluidsynth (SF2), windows-gs (today's live Windows GS Wavetable synth on PC22; never rendered). onset_ms = the library's own lead-in (first sample above -50 dBFS after a note-on, median over keys and velocities; measured by fetch's builder 22 Oct). velocity_gamma, gain_db, eq, resonance_db: starting values, calibrated by ear later. Rooms: ir = a 48 kHz float WAV under root; 4 channels = true stereo in the order L->L, L->R, R->L, R->R (Samplicity's Bricasti M7 quad files), 2 channels = mono in, stereo out; synth = the synthetic-IR fallback when ir is null or not installed; rt60_s/ir_t30_s = measured T30 (500 Hz-2 kHz, Schroeder) of the IR. Fetch blocks: url (or a BitTorrent magnet: fetch never downloads one, the archive must already be in root/_downloads under its cache name), sha256, bytes, unpack (zip|tar|7z|deb|none), subdir; optional strip (leading path parts dropped), members (fnmatch patterns kept), post (a recipe: bitklavier-sfz writes the SFZ map; sfz-wrap writes a wrapper SFZ beside the library's own, per its wrap block: global opcodes, set_cc defaults, replace = exact text fixes, see fetch.post_sfz_wrap). half_pedal: true passes CC64 raw to an SFZ that models half pedalling itself (else on/off at 64). copy_from = a local file copied in (the owner's own SoundFont).

steinway-b-162.label: Steinway B (Piano in 162)

fetch.source: BitTorrent only: ivyaudio.com/freebies (22 Oct 2026: 'Direct downloads will be back soon!'; the old $5 direct download is not used) gives this magnet for the SFZ edition (btih 4c1609b3098a309a32b6ce848dc3711b5182d9c9; the same magnet as the page's 2022 and 2025 Wayback copies; no official mirror on archive.org, GitHub or sfzinstruments). Fetched 22 Oct 2026 with aria2c 1.37 (Ubuntu deb, unpacked under engines_root/tools/aria2) from 7 DHT seeders: 4.9 GB in 2 min, every one of the 587 BitTorrent pieces checked, nothing uploaded, no seeding. fetch never downloads a magnet: the zip must already be in root/_downloads/ (57ebdd690cf6-Ivy_Audio_-_Piano_in_162_sfz.zip)

wrap.note: one take per note: the library's second round robin (2Close.flac) is mapped to the first, so sfizz loads 880 of its 1,760 samples (5.2 GB in memory instead of 10.0 GB: sfizz holds whole samples as float32, and up to 3 renders run at once); sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1), which also picks the pedal-down or pedal-up samples (locc64=64 / hicc64=63, read at the note-on); offset= on 136 samples whose attack came late: each now starts at most 1 ms before its first sound, with its main attack at most 10 ms in (before: up to 101 ms of silence in, 62 samples over 10 ms; measured 22 Oct on the files: first frame above -30 dB re the sample's peak, main attack -20 dB)

steinway-b-162.credit: Piano in 162 by Ivy Audio (Simon Dalzell): a Steinway Model B, every key sampled, 5 velocity layers, 2 round robins (one used here), separate pedal-down and pedal-up samples (the pedal-down ones ring with the other strings: real sympathetic resonance), recorded at 96 kHz with two pairs of Rode NT5s, a close pair inside the piano (used here) and an ambient pair in the hall (installed, not used); 24-bit/44.1 kHz FLAC, SFZ mapping by Marcelo Colina. No pedal or key-release noise samples. Free for personal and commercial use; redistribution prohibited without written consent (ivyaudio.com).

grand-c5.label: Grand piano (Yamaha C5)

wrap.note: the recommended flat sfz_live set with its sampled release, hammer noise, pedal noise and pedal resonance on at their recorded level (CC20-23 = 127, the author's recommended CC23 for Accurate; off by default); each pedal-noise take gets its own volume, 38 dB under the C4 velocity-64 note through sfizz (measured 22 Oct: down -26.9/-32.7, up -33.4/-39.7)

grand-c5.credit: Accurate-Salamander Grand Piano V6.2a by Chisato Yamauchi: a retuned, level-matched remaster of Alexander Holm's Salamander Grand Piano V3 (Yamaha C5), 16 velocity layers every minor third, hammer and string-resonance release samples, half pedal, pedal noise; sfz_live set, flat voicing, 48 kHz/24-bit FLAC. CC-BY.

bright-cf3.label: Bright concert grand (Yamaha CF3)

wrap.note: sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1); note_polyphony=1 moved from <global> to the main notes' <master> (on the release samples too, sfizz 1.2.3 left voices hanging at -94 dBFS after pedalled passages, so renders ran to the 30 s tail cap); the pedal and lid noises (Data/effect.txt, inlined) get a volume per take, 38 dB under the C4 velocity-64 note through sfizz (measured 22 Oct: sustain down -23.3/-22.2, up -38.2/-39.4; sostenuto down -31.1/-33.4, up -42.7/-39.1; the lid noise this SFZ plays on the soft pedal, CC67: open -5.2/-3.1, close -24.5/-14.2)

bright-cf3.credit: Maestro Concert Grand by Mats Helgesson (2003): an early-1990s Yamaha CF-3 sampled on every key, 5 velocity layers, Neumann KM84 X/Y pair, pedal up/down noise; SFZ by sfzinstruments. Free to use, not to sell or redistribute modified (mcgreadme.txt).

wrap.note: sustain pedal on/off at CC64 64, as General MIDI (sfizz's default threshold is 1); the two pedal-noise groups get hikey=-1 (they set lokey=-1 only, so sfizz also played pedal.on.wav on every key); the 30 key-release groups lose polyphony=1 (with it, sfizz 1.2.3 left release voices hanging at about -100 dBFS after pedalled passages, so renders ran to the 30 s tail cap); measured 22 Oct through sfizz against the C4 velocity-64 note: pedal down -32.1 and up -40.8 -> both -38; key-release noise follows velocity fully (amp_veltrack 100, +7.9 dB so velocity 64 stays at -38): after a velocity-20 note it was within 1-4 dB of that soft note in the treble, now 19+ dB under it
